tools.name: get_today
tools.description: Today's tasks from the user's active plan: the cardio and the strength exercises, each with its prescription and whether it is done, skipped or open. Every line carries the task id the write tools take.

tools.name: get_week
tools.description: The weekly training plan: one line per day with the cardio type, the strength type, and the day's status. Default is the current week.

tools.name: complete_task
tools.description: Mark one of today's tasks done: the cardio main task, the flexibility cooldown, or one strength exercise. The task id comes from get_today.

tools.name: skip_task
tools.description: Mark one task skipped (a skip still counts as resolved for the day; the cooldown is optional and needs no skip). The task id comes from get_today.

tools.name: unskip_task
tools.description: Undo a skip: the task returns to open. The task id comes from get_today.

tools.name: log_exercise
tools.description: Log one set of a strength exercise (reps, and the weight in pounds; 0 for bodyweight), and mark the exercise done. Repeat the call for the next sets.

tools.name: log_cardio
tools.description: Log the time of today's cardio main task (the timed swim or run), as MM:SS or seconds, and mark it done. For an interval day, pass rep_number to log one interval's time.

tools.name: log_pst
tools.description: Log a PST result (the Navy Physical Screening Test): 500-yard swim, 2-minute push-ups, 2-minute sit-ups, max pull-ups, 1.5-mile run. The new result recalibrates the daily plan.

tools.name: list_pst_results
tools.description: The user's PST results, newest first, each scored against the BUD/S minimums (the same scoring the PST results page shows).

tools.name: get_pst_result
tools.description: One PST result, scored against the BUD/S minimums.

tools.name: get_performance
tools.description: The performance page's numbers as text: the latest PST scored against the minimums, the PST history, and the plan's completion counts.

tools.name: upgrade
tools.description: Upgrade to Pro or Premium. Always two steps: without confirmPaymentSpend the tool only reads the exact price from Polar and charges nothing; call it again with confirmPaymentSpend: true to get the Polar checkout URL. The payment itself happens on Polar's page, never here.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "upgrade" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
